# Isla Primavera — streets & street businesses (tri-city focus)

**Chronicle:** Tropic Gooner ∪ Hunter — `campaigns/tropic-gooner/`.  
**Present lock:** `wb-tg-date` → **2019**.  
**Status:** bible draft, 2026-08-08. District faces and named venues from `LORE-BIBLE.md` / places-directory are **[canon]** where noted. Street names, block times, and new shop fronts are **[proposal]** until the GM promotes them.  
**Locks:** vibes spellings (**Jackedsonville**, city **Porto Lujara**, region may say Lujuria); no former-PC favor debts (`wb-tg-factions`); do not edit `regions-ui.json` or character registries from this file.  
**Companions:** `LORE-BIBLE.md` · `DRUGS.md` (White Sand / Quay Dust / Coral Nod · Bench Street · Humidor Annex · Float Barn 7) · `SOCIETY.md` · `REGIONS.md` · `reports/places-directory.md`.

---

## Canon status

- **[canon]** — district faces (Boardwalk Strip, Marina / Gilded Anchor, CiDance tower district, CRT substation block, PIU South edge; Carnaval Route, Lujara Docks, Ledger Row, Annex hill, Porto hills; The Row, The Quay, alleys, Main Street market, Book Nook block, Stadium edge). Named venues already in places-directory (Galaxy Fitness, Java Jump, CiDance, Neon Flux, casinos, pharmacies, Night Ledger, Dick's, RG's, Mar de Sabores, Bodega Roja, Book Nook, etc.).
- **[proposal]** — street names below that are not already locked as district labels; block walking times; new bodegas / chandlers / local shops; exact address numbers.
- **[open]** — promote/cut list at the end.

**How to read a street entry:** name → why it exists (belief → pressure → choice) → what sits on it → walking / drive notes. If a detail has no why, it is not here.

---

## Scale (tri-city bay) — [proposal unless noted]

Paradisio County's postcard money moves around the middle bay. The three cities are close enough that a night shift can end in one town and a second job start in another. They are far enough that you smell the diesel change.

| Leg | Typical time | Notes |
|-----|--------------|-------|
| Paradise Boardwalk ↔ CiDance Tower | **8–15 min** walk | Same tourist face; suite packs stay off the postcard strip [also in DRUGS] |
| Paradise Boardwalk ↔ Marina slips | **10–20 min** walk / **5 min** scooter | Colonnade shade until you hit the yacht fence |
| Paradise ↔ Lujara Docks | **35–55 min** drive off-peak; **70–90 min** Carnaval | Bay ring road [DRUGS] |
| Lujara Docks ↔ Ledger Row | **5–10 min** walk | Books meet barrels |
| CCC Annex hill ↔ Carnaval Route | **12–20 min** walk downhill | Culinary students in packs |
| Porto Lujara ↔ Jackedsonville Quay | **40–60 min** drive | Coastal or inland cut [DRUGS] |
| Quay front ↔ Casino Row | **8–15 min** walk | Neon spill between sets |
| Main Street market ↔ Book Nook block | **5–10 min** walk | Day market → gray retail strip |
| Any tri-city block (side street) | **2–4 min** per short block | Colonial grid is tight; mid-century towers break it |

**Block rule of thumb [proposal]:** old-quarter blocks are ~80–100 m facade to facade. A "ten-minute walk" is three to five blocks with shade stops. Mid-century tower lots eat two colonial blocks each.

---

## r01 — Paradise

North shore of the middle bay. Pastel colonial two-to-four story on the tourist face. Mid-century resort glass behind. Siesta is real. The city sells relaxation and staffs it with people who have not relaxed.

### Main arteries

#### Live Dream Boulevard — [proposal]

The booster-era bay frontage the chamber still puts on bus ads. Runs roughly parallel to the water from the boardwalk hotels toward the CiDance tower cluster. Four lanes, palm medians that die every dry season, bilingual tourism banners that CRT trucks use as wind breaks during festival drill.

**Why:** postwar boosters believed a mainland-style boulevard would pull cruise money inland. Pressure was sugar decline. Choice was pave the postcard road and name it after the slogan ("Live the Dream"). Locals shorten it to **Dream Blvd** and never say the full phrase without irony.

**On it:** CiDance Paradise Tower (buffet street entrance faces Dream; suite elevators face the service court) · mid-tier resort lobbies · scooter rental kiosks · one Dick's Grocery flagship with a tourist parking deck · RG's counter window in a strip mall notch (not Casa #43).

**Walk:** Boardwalk Strip gate to CiDance front doors ≈ **10–12 min** on the shaded arcade side.

#### Boardwalk Strip — [canon district label]

Wooden and concrete promenade on the water. Wristbands, taffy steam, licensed buskers. CRT festival crates sit near the substation end on purpose.

**Why (canon frame):** tourism math needs a walkable face the cameras can love. Street dealing here is career suicide; T0 Shore Gummies and Coolers are the licensed product (see DRUGS).

**On it:** Galaxy Fitness (local end, fluorescent banks visible through plate glass) · Java Jump flagship (morning white-collar line; deals are introductions, not bags) · T0 kiosks · hotel buffet overflow seating · DingLing Tea House cart hours on festival weeks [county chain, Paradise presence].

**Walk:** Galaxy Fitness → Java Jump ≈ **3–5 min**. Java Jump → CRT substation block ≈ **6–8 min**.

#### Anchor Way — [proposal]

The marina approach road. Ends at the Gilded Anchor Yacht Club gate and the slip parking that Kindred galas treat as Elysium driveway.

**Why:** yacht money needed a named approach that did not say "service road." Chamber chose Anchor. The club kept the word. The court kept the club.

**On it:** Gilded Anchor Yacht Club · slip chandlery (see Marina Service Alley) · valet stands · the unmarked gray Stevens van that somehow always finds a space.

### Student / service strip

#### Intern Loop (PIU South edge) — [proposal street name; PIU South campus is canon]

One-way shuttle loop and sidewalk strip where hospitality students change from class linen into hotel uniforms. Empanada cart at the gate is local lore in `entities.json`.

**Why:** hotels believed unpaid or underpaid intern labor would hold the fronts. Pressure is labor cost. Choice is evening classes so day shifts stay staffed (LORE-BIBLE). The road exists because shuttle buses needed a turnaround the city would paint.

**On it:** PIU South Campus gate · student laundromat · cheap knife-roll repair shop that also keys hotel badges "for a fee" · Casa Pharmacy #43 two blocks inland (wristband-optional neighborhood counter) · shared vans to Dream Blvd hotels.

**Walk:** Campus gate → Boardwalk Strip ≈ **15–20 min**. Campus → CiDance staff entrance ≈ **12–18 min**.

### Residential side streets

#### Calle San Aurelio — [proposal]

Older pastel row, named for the south-island saint the colonial parish reused everywhere. Laundry in courtyards. Scooters under tarps. Paint chalks to mint and coral pink.

**Why:** parish maps needed a street for the chapel walk. Boosters never renamed it because tourists do not come here. Locals keep the saint because the uncle's lease says so.

**On it:** walk-up apartments · a corner bodega (**Mercado del Sueño**, proposal) that sells ice, phone cards, and Dick's house-brand rice when the flagship is crowded · barber with a Bolero radio · no clubs.

#### Hibiscus Court — [proposal]

Cul-de-sac of small postwar bungalows behind the tower shadow. Quiet enough that Stevens vans feel wrong here.

**Why:** GI mainlanders wanted yards. County sold them cul-de-sacs. Tourism towers rose anyway. The court stayed because tearing it down costs more than the postcard needs.

### Industrial / service (marina)

#### Marina Service Alley — [proposal name; Humidor Annex already proposed in DRUGS]

Corrugated sheds behind the yacht fence. Fuel smell. Humidity cabinets behind a cigar-shop front.

**Why:** slips need fuel, ice, and linen. White Sand marina grade needs humidity. Belief: a cigar shop is a respectable front. Pressure: yacht clients pay for clean product. Choice: reseal room behind the humidor (DRUGS · Humidor Annex).

**On it:** The Humidor Annex [proposal] · small chandler (**Bayline Chandlery**, proposal) · ice house · laundry for boat linen.

### Alleys & control

#### Substation Lane — [proposal]

Short lane beside the Paradise CRT Substation. Black-and-coral trucks. Sonic-drill crates on festival weeks.

**Why:** CRT founding (2017) after a boardwalk tourist riot. Belief: visible gear calms donors. Pressure: viral clips. Choice: stage crates where tourists can photograph "safety."

**Architecture cue:** pastel arcade on the boardwalk side; concrete bunker face on the lane side. Same block, two islands.

## r02 — Porto Lujara (Lujuria region)

South curve of the bay. Colonial bones under neon. Working port that parties. Fried dough, diesel, brass rehearsal two streets over.

### Main arteries

#### Avenida del Carnaval (Carnaval Route) — [canon route / proposal formal name]

The waterfront parade street. Vendor stalls and float barns for months. After the parade, CRT runs the sweep and the asphalt remembers it was a road.

**Why:** city believed a named parade avenue would keep float traffic off the cargo gates. Pressure: cruise berth contracts hate blocked docks. Choice: one waterfront street owns the look-away week; the rest of the year it is trucks and brass practice.

**On it:** Float Barn 7 [proposal, DRUGS] · vendor stall pads · brass rehearsal lots · temporary T1 staging only during Carnaval week · no permanent club flagship (clubs sit one block inland).

**Walk:** Float barns → Lujara Docks gate ≈ **8–12 min**.

#### Muelle Road — [proposal]

Dock access road. Reefers, party-cruise unload, IFC cold-chain. Count ≠ manifest is a known tell.

**Why:** cargo needed a road that was not the parade route. Belief: separate fun from freight. Pressure: insurance and cruise optics. Choice: Muelle Road for barrels; Carnaval avenue for cameras.

**On it:** Lujara Docks gates · IFC cold-chain sheds · fuel pier · foremen offices with two clipboards (DRUGS architecture) · a 24h dock cafe (**Café Marejada**, proposal) open at 04:00 for dock coffee.

**Drive:** Docks → Ledger Row ≈ **5–10 min**.

#### Ledger Row — [canon district label]

Fluorescent office strip. Club-book accountants, union halls, chandlers. Night Ledger keeps offices here. Raid forecasts are a product.

**Why:** nightlife needed arithmetic that looked like daylight work. Pressure: CRT overtime and donor audits. Choice: put the books on a named office row, not above a club.

**On it:** Night Ledger Offices · La Pharmacy #120 (cash-only compounding) · union hall · marine insurance walk-ups · chandler storefronts that sell rope by day and invoice "consulting" by night.

### Student / service strip

#### Annex Hill Road — [proposal; CCC Culinary Annex is canon]

Switchback and stair cuts up to the Coastal Community College culinary annex. Knife rolls. Exhaustion that is half theater.

**Why:** college believed a hill campus would be cheaper land. Pressure: hotel catering demand. Choice: put students above the port so they walk down into suites that are not on tourist maps (LORE-BIBLE hook).

**On it:** CCC Culinary Annex · student canteen · secondhand whites shop · shared scooter rack · catering van lot.

**Walk:** Annex → Ledger Row ≈ **15–25 min** downhill / longer up.

### Residential

#### Calle de las Abuelas — [proposal]

Hillside street of bought-out and not-yet-bought-out houses. Development Consortium "green condo" signs face the older pastel facades.

**Why:** developers believed hillside views sell. Pressure: tourism spillover rent. Choice: buy out elders. Soil studies stay "forthcoming." Locals named the street after the aunts, not the city map (map may still say a booster number).

**On it:** family houses · a parish hall · one remaining corner store (**Tienda Lujara**, proposal).

### Industrial / dock strip (extra)

#### Barrel Court — [proposal]

Dead-end yard behind the cold-chain. Corrugated, no neon, bad for Instagram. Good for reseal talk that never reaches Night Ledger's clean clipboard.

**Why:** false bulkheads need a court trucks can reverse into. Belief: invisible yards are safer than pretty streets. Pressure: count mismatch risk. Choice: keep Barrel Court off tourism maps.

### Alleys

#### Brass Alley — [proposal]

Behind float barns. Horn practice leaks. After Carnaval, CRT sweep staging. Off-season: kids and cats.

**Why:** floats need a back path that is not the parade camera line. Named for the sound, not a saint.

## r03 — Jackedsonville (Crimson Quay region)

West of the bay. Casinos first; city grew around the carpets. Locals say the Quay for the harbor. The 2014 city rename failed. The waterfront kept Crimson Quay. Spell the city **Jackedsonville**.

### Main arteries

#### Carpet Mile (The Row) — [proposal nickname; The Row is canon district]

Casino strip road. Crimson Oasis polished floor on one side. Red Fortune themed nights on the other. Carpet smell is its own category.

**Why:** shareholders believed a continuous carpet frontage would keep gamblers from seeing daylight exits. Pressure: cruise day-trips and spring festival. Choice: build the Mile as one lit canyon. Locals say carpet names, not "the casino" (LORE-BIBLE stereotype).

**On it:** Crimson Oasis Casino · Red Fortune · tourist sportsbooks · a Dick's Grocery that never sleeps and sells microwave meals to people who lost their dinner money · Rough Ride storefront security desk (legitimate money's door).

**Walk:** Oasis doors → Quay club doors ≈ **8–15 min**.

#### Quay Front / Quay Street — [canon harbor face; proposal formal "Quay Street"]

Harborfront club district. Neon Flux is the anchor room. Quay Nights fills the street each spring. Licensed-club truce holds while the lights stay on.

**Why:** harbor already moved cargo. Club money believed neon on the water sells harder than inland rooms. Pressure: 2014 viral alley clip and failed rebrand. Choice: push the loud legal face onto Quay Street and push T2 into stairs and reseal rooms (DRUGS · Bench Street).

**On it:** Neon Flux · The Red Mirror (bar) · club queue barriers · fog-machine ozone · El Pharmacy #35 a short block off the neon (noon shutters; Quay Dust rumor after dark).

#### Main Street — [canon district: Main Street market]

Daytime fusion stalls, grill smoke, mango, ceviche. Night: different crowd, same asphalt.

**Why:** market vendors believed the casino workers needed lunch that was not buffet steam. Pressure: day shift money. Choice: keep Main Street as the mortal stomach of the city while the Row sells fantasy.

**On it:** Mar de Sabores (sit-down catch of the day) · Bodega Roja (sandwiches under digital billboards) · fruit stalls · a Java Jump satellite kiosk (not the Paradise flagship) · RG's window in a strip corner.

### Alleys & gray retail

#### Bench Street — [proposal; already in DRUGS as Bench Street Reseal]

Behind Neon Flux. Galvanized door painted coral. Quay Dust press and bag. Stairwells shared with the Renta-Girl cluster's paper trail.

**Why:** Tithe tax and Quay Rojo margin need a street that does not photograph well. Belief: coral paint blends with CRT trucks (DRUGS). Pressure: alley skim and tax raises. Choice: reseal here, not on Quay Front.

**On it:** Bench Street Reseal [proposal] · unmarked speakeasy doors · Renta-Girl alley cluster (licensed shell / unlicensed roster) · dumpsters that Stevens teams know by barcode.

#### Book Nook Block (gray strip) — [canon district face]

Legal retail by day. Screens drift stranger after dark. Nelly's bookstore keeps late hours.

**Why:** county needs a place that looks like commerce for audits. Pressure: adult retail and research rabbit holes. Choice: concentrate gray tabs on one strip so the Row stays postcard-clean enough for shareholders.

**On it:** Nelly's Book Nook · phone-repair / SIM stalls · a pawn that buys festival jewelry · print shop that will do flyers and will not ask.

### Student / service (stadium edge)

#### Scholarship Drive — [proposal; Stadium edge is canon]

Road past the multi-purpose stadium and sports clubs. Gang-sponsored scholarships are thickest here (LORE-BIBLE).

**Why:** clubs believed stadium adjacency buys legitimacy. Pressure: youth idle risk and sponsor optics. Choice: put gyms and clubhouses on one drive the county can point at in brochures.

**On it:** stadium gates · sports clubhouses · a Galaxy Fitness franchise satellite (proposal presence; Paradise flagship remains primary) · protein-shake carts · bus stops for night-shift casino dealers.

### Residential

#### Coral Nod Lane — [proposal name; Coral Nod is the T2 opioid street name from DRUGS]

Quiet tenement street inland of the alleys. Not a dealing bazaar. The nickname stuck after an OD year the county reclassified as "heat illness" on tourism weeks. Locals use it as a warning, not a brand.

**Why:** belief (skewed): if you name the street after the fear, kids stay off it. Pressure: T2 dens need doors away from Quay cameras. Choice: dens in walk-ups; CRT prefers TV busts on prettier blocks. **Do not** put a Coral Nod shopfront here — the product is private dens, not a menu board.

**On it:** walk-ups · a church basement · laundromat · no neon.

### Industrial / dock strip

#### Slip Shed Road — [proposal]

Corrugated harbor sheds west of the club lights. Fishing ice by day. Quiet handoffs by arrangement. Not Lujara's primary import node; Jackedsonville's sheds are the last mile.

**Why:** Quay clubs need ice and power. Traffickers need a shed that smells like fish. Pressure: Paradise and Porto watch the big manifests. Choice: small last-mile here.

**On it:** ice sheds · generator cages for Quay Nights · a chandler (**Quay Cordage**, proposal) · no casino logos.

## Architecture cues (stay on-model)

- **Old quarter:** seafoam / coral pink / butter yellow / mint; chalking paint; colonnades; hurricane shutters; clay tile or corrugated tin; wet-stone courtyards.
- **Resort / casino:** mid-century concrete, tired glass, corporate tiki leftovers, carpet canyons.
- **Docks:** corrugated sheds, reefers, crane shadows, diesel.
- **Signage:** bilingual English/Spanish default; Tagalog / Vietnamese / Creole hand lettering in markets; neon on the Row and Quay; hand-painted rum/lottery ads inland.
- **Machines:** land-yacht sedans, 80s Japanese imports, scooters, resort shuttles, black-and-coral CRT trucks, barcode-only Stevens vans.
